topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how local treatment can eliminate tumours and why its success depends on tumour accessibility and extent.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how cytotoxic drugs kill cancer cells and why their effectiveness is constrained by toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking hormone signalling suppresses cancers that remain dependent on it for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing cell cycle checkpoint functions create vulnerabilities that treatments can selectively exploit.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting a complementary DNA repair mechanism selectively kills BRCA-deficient cancer cells.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how identifying the oncogenic activity sustaining a tumour enables treatment directed against that activity.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitor resistance and long-term treatment limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why kinase inhibition often becomes ongoing disease management rather than a cure.

topics.label: Antibody-directed cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibody recognition of cancer cell surface proteins directs therapeutic effects towards those cells.

topics.label: Evidence for cancer immune surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic evaluates whether the body's existing immune responses protect against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint blockade and tumour antigen recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how releasing inhibitory signals can restore antitumour T cell activity and why tumour neoantigens influence the response.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapies that deliberately give T cells the ability to engage and kill selected cancer cells.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided selection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why variable treatment responses require better ways to match patients to effective therapies.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how prevention and earlier diagnosis complicate the attribution of improved cancer outcomes to treatment.

topics.label: Future cancer care priorities and treatment dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how future improvements in cancer care must be weighed against established survival benefits and patients' quality of life.
